resumen: The king of Jericho learned about the spies and ordered Rahab to hand them over. A letter for when pressure hits all at once.

versos.texto: The king of Jericho was told, “Behold, men of the children of Israel came in here tonight to spy out the land.”
Jericho’s king sent to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who have come to you, who have entered into your house; for they have come to spy out all the land.”

reflexion: Yesterday we met Rahab. Today the news travels fast: that same night someone alerts the king of Jericho. The king has already received word that men of Israel have come to spy out the land. The king sends Rahab an order: to bring out the men who have come into her house.

Now the pressure falls on her. The king of her city demands that she bring out her guests. These verses do not yet say what she will answer. They leave us in that moment of tension. Maybe you know that feeling: a demand that comes suddenly and forces you to decide.

Sometimes pressure comes from work, from family or from what others expect. In those moments you are not alone. God sees what happens in your house, even at night. You can stop, breathe and ask Him for wisdom before you answer. You can also talk with someone you trust; you don't have to carry that burden alone.
dedicatoria: This letter is for you, who feel pressure on every side today. You don't have to face it alone.
oracion: Lord, you see every difficult night and every demand that presses on us. Give us calm and wisdom to know what to do, and trust in your care. In Jesus' name, amen.
